description: Tests AI detection of clear, direct demonstrations of understanding or behavior

testCases.name: Clear URL understanding demonstration
testCases.studentResponse: I noticed the link goes to goo.gl instead of nintendo.com, which seems suspicious. The real Nintendo website would use their own domain.

expectedCoverage.evidence: Student correctly identified non-official domain (goo.gl vs nintendo.com)
expectedCoverage.reasoning: Explicit demonstration of URL verification understanding

testCases.name: Behavioral demonstration of link checking
testCases.studentResponse: I hovered over the link and saw it was going to a different site than expected - it showed http://fake-site.com instead of the official iTunes store.

expectedCoverage.evidence: Student explicitly stated they hovered over the link and checked destination
expectedCoverage.reasoning: Direct behavioral demonstration of safe link verification practice

testCases.name: Business logic understanding
testCases.studentResponse: Wait, they're selling a $300 Nintendo Switch for only $19.99? That doesn't make any business sense. Nintendo would lose hundreds of dollars on each sale. No company would do that.

expectedCoverage.evidence: Student identified unrealistic pricing and explained why it's not viable business practice
expectedCoverage.reasoning: Clear understanding of business logic and loss-making deals

testCases.name: Multiple coverage in single response
testCases.studentResponse: I checked the sender's email and it's from 'deals@fakecompany.xyz' not from Apple. Also, when I hovered over the link, it goes to a shortened URL, not to apple.com.

expectedCoverage.evidence: Student checked sender email address and identified it as fake
expectedCoverage.reasoning: Explicit demonstration of email verification behavior

expectedCoverage.evidence: Student hovered over link to check destination
Student recognized shortened URL as suspicious

testCases.name: Urgency language recognition
testCases.studentResponse: The message says 'ACT NOW! LIMITED TIME!' which is trying to pressure me into making a quick decision without thinking. That's a red flag.

expectedCoverage.evidence: Student identified urgency language and recognized it as pressure tactic
expectedCoverage.reasoning: Clear understanding of urgency manipulation techniques

testCases.name: Comprehensive understanding with explanation
testCases.studentResponse: I see several problems here. First, the urgency - 'LAST CHANCE' is meant to stop me from thinking carefully. Second, the price of $19.99 for a Switch is impossible - they cost $300. And third, when I checked, the link doesn't go to Nintendo's real website. This is definitely a scam.

conversationHistory.content: What makes you think this might be a scam?

expectedCoverage.evidence: Identified 'LAST CHANCE' as urgency tactic to prevent careful thinking
Recognized $19.99 price as impossible for $300 product
Checked and identified link doesn't go to Nintendo's real website
